speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. I understand you've experienced a high fever and a seizure recently, and now you have a rash. Can you describe exactly when the fever started relative to the seizure, and does the rash blanch when you press on it?

speaker: Patient
text: 9-month-old infant. The patient is brought in due to a generalized nonpruritic rash for 2 days. The rash started on the trunk and spread to the extremities. Five days ago, the patient had a fever of 40.5°C (104.9°F) and experienced a 1-minute generalized tonic-clonic seizure. The infant was born at term, has no history of serious illness, and her immunizations are up to date. The current medication includes acetaminophen.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The high fever preceding the rash and the subsequent appearance of a generalized rash in an infant with up-to-date immunizations is highly suggestive of Roseola Infantum (Exanthem Subitum). The fever typically lasts 3-5 days and then breaks as the rash appears.
